verdicts.decision_note: The client introduces reducing the E and L scale relative to the second V's left arm.
Target-specific first implementation claim for the requested E and L scale reduction.
First concrete post-claim failure: the surrounding letters still make the second V appear noticeably smaller.
The client replaces the approximate scale reference with exact alignment to the second V's left-arm height.
Target-specific post-modification claim that the E and L cap height now matches the second V's left arm.
The client ends the project and explicitly prohibits further design revisions, removing this design obligation.

source_message.speaker: freelancer
source_message.text:
Hi Brittany,

Here is the proof built strictly around the proportional mathematical system you outlined!

True Proportional Reduction: The second V is built as a pure proportional scale of the Hero V (no redrawing or stroke modifications), preserving its exact geometry, character, and sweeping right arm.

Cap-Height Alignment: The E and L forms have been scaled so their top line anchors flush to the top tip of the second V's left arm.

Natural Signature Overhang: As a result of this proportional scale, the second V's right arm naturally extends slightly above the alphabet line as our signature detail.

Common Baseline & Geometry: Built on our winning Variation B tight kerning with both V's resting flush on the common baseline, and the É accent confirmed as a direct clone of the Hero V's sweep.

I think establishing this mathematical hierarchy tied the entire identity together beautifully. Let me know if this delivers the exact balance you were looking for so we can lock in the master assets

execution.observed_behavior: Freelancer reports rescaling the E and L forms so their top line aligns with the second V's left arm in the rebuilt proportional system.
